    // Re-checks the current request's tenant database for pending migrations
    // periodically, not just once per app-domain lifetime. AutoRunMigrationsOnStartup
    // (and the old one-time version of this check) only ever look at the
    // migration files that existed at the moment the app pool started/first
    // resolved that tenant - a file added afterward to a long-running process
    // was never picked up until the next full restart. Covers both multi-tenant
    // (keyed per resolved client) and legacy single-database mode (one fixed key).
    private static readonly System.Collections.Concurrent.ConcurrentDictionary<string, DateTime> _tenantMigrationsLastChecked =
        new System.Collections.Concurrent.ConcurrentDictionary<string, DateTime>();

    private static readonly TimeSpan MigrationRecheckInterval = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2);

    private void RunTenantMigrationsOnce()
    {
        TenantClientInfo client = DbConnectionFactory.GetCurrentClient();
        string key = client?.ClientCode ?? "__legacy__";

        DateTime now = DateTime.UtcNow;
        if (_tenantMigrationsLastChecked.TryGetValue(key, out DateTime lastChecked) &&
            now - lastChecked < MigrationRecheckInterval)
        {
            return;
        }

        _tenantMigrationsLastChecked[key] = now;

        try
        {
            DatabaseMigrationRunner.RunPendingForCurrentClient();
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            // The key is NOT removed on failure: removing it made every following request - every
            // image, script and popup callback - re-run the failing migration and log it again
            // (HR-UGANDA: dozens of times a minute, each holding the request up). A failed
            // migration is retried after the normal interval instead.
            // Trace.TraceError alone goes nowhere on a deployed server (no listener is
            // configured), so a failing migration was invisible - and because the runner
            // stops at the first failure, every later script silently never applied. That
            // is how a server ends up missing the dynamic-menu schema. ErrorLogHelper
            // swallows its own failures, so this cannot make the request worse.
            ErrorLogHelper.Log(ex, "Global.PerTenantMigration");
            System.Diagnostics.Trace.TraceError("Per-tenant migration check failed for " + key + ": " + ex);
        }
    }

    // Probation "ends in a month" reminders (ProbationReminderService). The app has no scheduler,
    // so - like the migration check above - this rides on requests: at most once every few hours
    // per database, on a background thread so no page ever waits on a mail server. Checking more
    // often than needed is harmless: HR_ProbationReminderLog allows one reminder per probation
    // end date. Nothing is sent until SmtpHost / MailFromAddress are set in Web.config.
    // Switch off with <add key="ProbationReminderAutoRun" value="false" />.
    private static readonly System.Collections.Concurrent.ConcurrentDictionary<string, DateTime> _probationRemindersLastChecked =
        new System.Collections.Concurrent.ConcurrentDictionary<string, DateTime>();

    private static readonly TimeSpan ProbationReminderInterval = TimeSpan.FromHours(6);

    private void RunProbationRemindersInBackground()
    {
        if (string.Equals(ConfigurationManager.AppSettings["ProbationReminderAutoRun"], "false", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            return;

        TenantClientInfo client = DbConnectionFactory.GetCurrentClient();
        string key = client?.ClientCode ?? "__legacy__";

        DateTime now = DateTime.UtcNow;
        if (_probationRemindersLastChecked.TryGetValue(key, out DateTime lastChecked) &&
            now - lastChecked < ProbationReminderInterval)
        {
            return;
        }

        _probationRemindersLastChecked[key] = now;

        // Resolved here, on the request thread: the tenant lookup needs HttpContext.
        string connectionString = DbConnectionFactory.GetConnectionString();
        MailSettings settings = MailSettings.FromConfig();

        System.Web.Hosting.HostingEnvironment.QueueBackgroundWorkItem(delegate (System.Threading.CancellationToken token)
        {
            try
            {
                ProbationReminderService.RunDue(connectionString, "Auto", null, null, settings, DateTime.Today);
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                // Left in the throttle on purpose: a database or mail problem is retried at the
                // next interval, not on every request.
                ErrorLogHelper.Log(ex, "Global.ProbationReminders");
            }
        });
    }

    void Application_Error(object sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        var context = HttpContext.Current;
        if (context == null) return;

        var exception = context.Server.GetLastError();
        if (exception == null) return;

        string path = context.Request.AppRelativeCurrentExecutionFilePath ?? string.Empty;
        if (UserSessionHelper.IsPublicRequestPath(path)) return;

        // Only bounce to SignIn when the user is actually logged out / session expired.
        // Do not treat normal page/SQL errors as logout.
        bool sessionMissing = context.Session == null || !UserSessionHelper.IsRequestAuthenticated(context);
        if (sessionMissing || UserSessionHelper.IsSessionExpiredError(exception))
        {
            // Log BEFORE clearing. This branch used to swallow the exception entirely,
            // which made a broken session store indistinguishable from a normal expiry:
            // if dbo.HR_SessionState is missing or unreadable on a customer server, the
            // session provider throws here on every request, the user is bounced back to
            // SignIn straight after a successful login, and nothing was recorded anywhere.
            // A null Session is the tell - a genuine expiry has a live (empty) Session.
            // Log every exception reaching this branch, not only a null Session: a real
            // failure during sign-in (before the user is authenticated) also lands here and
            // used to leave no trace, only a redirect saying the session ended.
            ErrorLogHelper.Log(exception, context.Session == null
                ? "Global.SessionStoreUnavailable"
                : "Global.ErrorTreatedAsSessionExpired");

            context.Server.ClearError();
            UserSessionHelper.RedirectToSignIn(context, UserSessionHelper.SessionEndReason.Expired);
            return;
        }

        // A genuine application error (not a logout). Record the full technical
        // detail centrally (type/message/stack/inner + user/company/page), then
        // let <customErrors> render the generic ErrorPage - the customer never
        // sees the real message. Do NOT ClearError here so customErrors kicks in.
        ErrorLogHelper.Log(exception, "Application_Error");
    }

    protected void Application_PostAuthorizeRequest()
    {
        var path = HttpContext.Current.Request.Path.ToLower();

        // DevExpress handler endpoints need session state so that:
        //   - Report Viewer (DXXRDV.axd) can retrieve the OpenReport() document from session.
        //   - Report Designer (DXXRD.axd) can access user/company context.
        //   - Query Builder (DXQB.axd) and Dashboard (DXDD.axd) behave consistently.
        // Without this, IIS does not allocate session state for .axd handlers, causing
        // DevExpress to throw "document not found" errors that bubble up as sign-in redirects.
        if (path.Contains("dxxrdv.axd") ||   // Web Document Viewer
            path.Contains("dxxrd.axd")  ||   // Report Designer
            path.Contains("dxqb.axd")   ||   // Query Builder
            path.Contains("dxdd.axd")   ||   // Dashboard
            path.Contains("dxr.axd")    ||   // legacy DX handler (kept for compatibility)
            path.Contains("dashboard"))
        {
            HttpContext.Current.SetSessionStateBehavior(
                System.Web.SessionState.SessionStateBehavior.Required
            );
        }
    }

    private void ASPxWebControl_CallbackError(object sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        var context = HttpContext.Current;
        if (context == null) return;

        Exception exception = context.Server.GetLastError();
        if (exception == null) return;

        string path = context.Request.AppRelativeCurrentExecutionFilePath ?? string.Empty;

        // Do NOT redirect resource/handler requests (.axd, .css, .js, etc.) to sign-in —
        // these are background requests from DevExpress controls and a null session on them
        // is normal when the session state fix above has not yet been applied or the request
        // genuinely has no session. Show the DevExpress error message instead.
        if (UserSessionHelper.IsPublicRequestPath(path))
        {
            DevExpress.Web.ASPxWebControl.SetCallbackErrorMessage(exception.Message);
            return;
        }

        bool sessionMissing = context.Session == null || !UserSessionHelper.IsRequestAuthenticated(context);

        if (sessionMissing || UserSessionHelper.IsSessionExpiredError(exception))
        {
            // Same reasoning as Application_Error above: a null Session means the session
            // STORE failed, not that the user's login expired - record it instead of
            // silently bouncing to SignIn with no evidence.
            // Log every exception reaching this branch, not only a null Session: a real
            // failure during sign-in (before the user is authenticated) also lands here and
            // used to leave no trace, only a redirect saying the session ended.
            ErrorLogHelper.Log(exception, context.Session == null
                ? "Global.SessionStoreUnavailable"
                : "Global.ErrorTreatedAsSessionExpired");

            context.Server.ClearError();
            UserSessionHelper.RedirectToSignIn(context, UserSessionHelper.SessionEndReason.Expired);
            return;
        }

        // A genuine application error on a callback. Log the full detail centrally
        // and show the customer a generic message. The real message is shown only
        // for local requests (server-side debugging via localhost) - never to a
        // remote customer.
        ErrorLogHelper.Log(exception, "CallbackError");
        string callbackMessage = context.Request.IsLocal ? exception.Message : ErrorLogHelper.FriendlyMessage;
        DevExpress.Web.ASPxWebControl.SetCallbackErrorMessage(callbackMessage);
    }

    void Session_End(object sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        if (HttpContext.Current != null)
        {
            EditLockHelper.ReleaseAllForSession(HttpContext.Current);
            UserSessionHelper.DeactivateFromEndingSession(HttpContext.Current);
        }
    }
    void Application_PreRequestHandlerExecute(object sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        ThemeHelper.ApplyToCurrentRequest();

        var page = HttpContext.Current?.CurrentHandler as System.Web.UI.Page;
        if (page == null) return;

        page.Init += delegate
        {
            SqlDataSourceConnectionBinder.Apply(page);
        };

        page.Load += delegate
        {
            SqlDataSourceConnectionBinder.Apply(page);
        };

        page.PreRender += delegate
        {
            SqlDataSourceConnectionBinder.Apply(page);
        };
    }

    void Application_AcquireRequestState(object sender, EventArgs e)
    {
        var context = HttpContext.Current;
        if (context?.Session == null) return;

        ApplyCompanyNumberGrouping(context);

        if (!UserSessionHelper.EnsureAuthenticatedOrRedirect(context)) return;
    }

    // Amount grouping follows the connected company's currency (INR = Indian
    // lakh/crore, otherwise international). Applied per request so the Customised
    // Reports grid and the DevExpress designed reports (which format with
    // "{0:#,##0.00}") both group correctly. Only NumberGroupSizes is changed.
    void ApplyCompanyNumberGrouping(HttpContext context)
    {
        try
        {
            var session = context.Session;
            object cid = session["CompanyID"];
            int companyId;
            if (cid == null || !int.TryParse(Convert.ToString(cid), out companyId) || companyId <= 0)
                return;

            // Cache the currency per company in session (avoid a DB hit each request).
            object cachedCompany = session["__GroupCompanyId"];
            string currency = session["__GroupCurrency"] as string;
            if (currency == null || cachedCompany == null || Convert.ToInt32(cachedCompany) != companyId)
            {
                currency = CurrencyFormatHelper.CurrencyForCompany(companyId) ?? string.Empty;
                session["__GroupCurrency"] = currency;
                session["__GroupCompanyId"] = companyId;
            }

            CurrencyFormatHelper.Apply(currency);
        }
        catch { /* non-critical: leave the default culture */ }
    }

content.text:
Right — that flips the direction of compatibility, and I think that's the correct call. The legacy host/port resolution is a hack (a public port per customer, `X-Forwarded-Port` sniffing, falling back to `sqlConnectionString` when it can't match). Our key-based resolution is strictly better, and there should be one catalog with one owner: us.

So the seam becomes: **we own `HR_Master` and issue the keys; legacy stores its key in `Web.config` and asks us.** Legacy's `DbConnectionFactory.ResolveClientByHost` gets replaced by a resolve-by-key call to our API, and its `EnableMultiTenant`/port registry path becomes the fallback for servers not yet migrated.

Two decisions shape what I build, so let me settle them before writing code.

questions.question: When legacy presents its product key to our API, what comes back?

options.label: Tenant identity only (Recommended)
options.description: We return ClientCode + DatabaseName + status. Legacy builds the connection string locally from its existing `clientConnectionTemplate` in Web.config — code it already has in BuildClientConnectionString. No SQL credentials ever cross the network, and a compromised API leaks database names, not logins.

options.label: Full connection string
options.description: We return the whole connection string, AES-encrypted with the shared key. Simpler for legacy — no per-server template to maintain, and each tenant can sit on a different SQL server. But our API becomes a credential distributor and the string crosses the wire on every cache miss.
options.preview:
POST /api/Tenant/Resolve
  { productKey: "SO1-7K2M-..." }

200 {
  clientCode:     "ACME",
  databaseName:   "HR_ACME",
  connectionString: "<AES blob>",
  isActive:       true
}

Legacy then:
  aes.Decrypt(resp.connectionString, KEY)

→ full SQL credentials transit HTTP
→ tenants can live on different servers

questions.question: How much of legacy moves over in this phase?

options.label: Tenant resolution only (Recommended)
options.description: Legacy keeps its own SignIn page, session and JwtHelper — we only replace how it picks a database. Small, surgical change to DbConnectionFactory, kills the port-per-customer deployment. Auth delegation becomes a later phase once the catalog is proven.
options.preview:
CHANGED in legacy:
  App_Code/DbConnectionFactory.cs
    ResolveClientByHost(hostKeys)
      → ResolveClientByProductKey(key)
  Web.config
    + <add key="ProductKey" value="SO1-..." />
    + <add key="TenantApiBaseUrl" ... />

UNTOUCHED:
  SignIn.aspx, UserSessionHelper,
  JwtHelper, session bootstrap,
  company selection

≈ 1 file + config

options.label: Resolution + full auth delegation
options.description: Legacy also posts credentials to our login endpoint and builds its ASP.NET session from our JWT response. One authentication system across both apps. Much larger blast radius: SignIn.aspx, UserSessionHelper, JwtHelper, session bootstrap and company selection all change, and a login outage on our side takes legacy down with it.
options.preview:
CHANGED in legacy:
  App_Code/DbConnectionFactory.cs
  App_Code/UserSessionHelper.cs
  App_Code/JwtHelper.cs
  App_Code/AuthHelper.cs
  Account/SignIn.aspx(.cs)
  Global.asax session bootstrap
  + company-selection flow

→ one auth system, both apps
→ our API outage = legacy cannot log in

≈ 6+ files, touches every login

SolutionOne — DB Migration Runner
=================================

SolutionOneDbMigrator.exe runs a folder of .sql scripts (tables, columns, stored
procedures, views, data fixes) against one database you name, and records what ran
in dbo.HR_SchemaMigrationHistory — including the last query each script executed.

This folder is part of the web site only so the tool is published with it. On the
server it lands in:

    C:\Publish\RunScripts\SolutionOneDbMigrator.exe

Just double-click it there. It finds the deployed scripts on its own — it looks for
..\App_Data\DbMigrations next to itself, i.e. C:\Publish\App_Data\DbMigrations — so
the folder box is already filled in. Enter the database name (or press "Load list"),
then press "Run all scripts".

The web.config in this folder blocks HTTP access, so the exe cannot be downloaded
from the site. Do not remove it.

Source and full documentation: C:\Project\Tools\DbMigrationRunner\README.md
=== migrations README ===
# HR Payroll DB Migrations

Place incremental SQL files in this folder. Files run in filename order and are recorded once per client database in `dbo.HR_SchemaMigrationHistory`.

Recommended naming:

```text
001_Add_UserTheme.sql
002_Menu_Restructure.sql
003_Attendance_Import.sql
```

Rules:

- Do not include `USE [DatabaseName]`; the runner connects to the correct client database.
- Keep scripts SQL Server 2014 compatible.
- Use `GO` between batches when needed; the runner supports `GO`.
- Make each script safe to run inside a transaction.
- Do not put the full baseline schema here for existing DBs. Use the full schema only when creating a new client database.

You're right, and it's already true today — this isn't something multi-tenancy introduces. Your own `appsettings.json` says so:

> Password encryption must stay byte-for-byte compatible with the sibling hr_payroll project — both read/write `HR_UserMaster.PasswordHash` in the same database.

One database per customer, two applications on it. The new backend's 345 entities were scaffolded from the same schema legacy writes to.

## That actually strengthens the choice you just made

Identity-only is right for a second reason beyond "payroll has no business knowing": **the two apps connect with different credentials.** Legacy uses `sa1` from `clientConnectionTemplate`; the backend uses whatever is in its AES-encrypted `WebPortalConnectionString`. If the catalog handed out one connection string, you'd be forcing both apps onto a single SQL login and losing the ability to give the backend a restricted one.

Identity-only lets them **agree on `InitialCatalog` while keeping their own credentials.** That's exactly the seam you want.

It also fixes a live bug. `DbConnectionFactory` carries this comment:

> ...keeps single-tenant requests from ever opening HR_Master — which the app pool identity (e.g. `IIS APPPOOL\HR`) has no rights to, causing "Cannot open database 'HR_Master' requested by the login".

Once legacy resolves over HTTP, it needs **no rights on the catalog at all.** That failure mode disappears.

And: **one key per tenant, not per app.** The key identifies the customer. Both apps present the same key and get the same `DatabaseName` back. Two keys for one database would be a split-brain waiting to happen.

## The thing that actually needs deciding

Shared database + two apps means **two migration systems writing to one schema, with nothing reconciling them.** This is the real consequence, and it's already biting you:

| | Legacy | New backend |
|---|---|---|
| Folder | `App_Data/DbMigrations` | `SolutionOne_DataAccessLayer/SqlScripts` |
| Count | 239 files | 143 files |
| Naming | `251_LoanDirectPayment.sql` | `Update_CanteenMealSession_Rates_20261022.sql` |
| Tracked in | `dbo.HR_SchemaMigrationHistory` (checksummed) | **nowhere** |
| Applied | **automatically, every 2 min per tenant**, from `Global.asax` | by hand |

Legacy's runner walks `GetActiveClients()` and auto-applies to **every active client database on a timer.** The backend's scripts are applied manually, tracked nowhere, and the two sequences already interleave in practice — your own backend comments reference "script 035/036" meaning SolutionOneWeb 239/240.

With one customer that's an annoyance you've absorbed. With N customers it's a production hazard: legacy silently migrates all N databases unattended while backend scripts land per-customer by hand, drift is guaranteed, and the EF model throws `Invalid column name` on whichever tenant is behind — for one customer only, with no signal.

Adding a tenant catalog on top of that doesn't fix it. It multiplies it.

## What I'd do

**One sequence, one history table, one runner.**

`HR_SchemaMigrationHistory` is already the right table — it exists on every customer DB, it has checksums, and `SolutionOneDbMigrator.exe` already drives it. Adopt it for both apps:

- Backend scripts get renumbered into the **same shared sequence** as legacy, not a parallel one with a prefix. Order across the boundary matters — a backend script depending on a legacy column has to run after it, and a separate sequence can't express that.
- The backend gets a runner reading the same table and skipping what's applied.
- `SchemaVersion` in the catalog = highest applied migration, returned by `/Resolve` (already in the contract you picked). Both apps refuse to serve a tenant whose version is below what their build requires — so a behind-schema customer gets a clean "upgrade pending" instead of a column error three screens deep.

**Who runs it** is the open question, and I'd pick: the **external migrator at provisioning and upgrade time**, driven by the service portal. `SolutionOneDbMigrator.exe` already does this against a named database.

The alternative — leaving legacy's `Global.asax` auto-runner on — means the legacy payroll app is unattendedly migrating databases the new backend depends on, on customer servers, triggered by whoever happens to browse a page. That's fine as a single-tenant convenience and genuinely bad as a fleet operation. I'd turn `AutoRunMigrationsOnStartup` off as part of this work and make migration an explicit, logged step in the subscription flow you already have.

That does mean the service portal grows a responsibility: provision DB → run migrations → register in catalog → issue key. Which is the right place for it, since it already creates the database.

So before I write code: **do you want the migration consolidation in this phase, or do you want the catalog + key switch first and migrations kept as-is for now?** I'd do the catalog first and migrations immediately after — they're separable, and the catalog is useless without tenants to put in it. But I wouldn't onboard customer #2 before both are done.

/* ============================================================================================
   TENANT CATALOGUE - product key resolution
   ============================================================================================

   *** RUN THIS AGAINST HR_Master, NOT A CUSTOMER DATABASE ***

   Every other script in this folder targets a tenant's own database. This one targets the shared
   catalogue that says which database each customer uses. Running it against a tenant database
   creates a dead HR_ClientProductKey table there and nothing will work.

   HR_ClientRegistry is shared with the legacy SolutionOneWeb payroll app, which selects
   ClientID, ClientCode, HostName, DatabaseName, ConnectionString WHERE IsActive = 1
   (see SolutionOneWeb/App_Code/DbConnectionFactory.cs). Everything below is additive so those
   queries keep working unchanged on a server that has not been upgraded yet.

   Idempotent - safe to re-run.
   ============================================================================================ */

SET NOCOUNT ON;
GO

/* Guard against the most likely mistake: running this on a tenant database. HR_UserMaster only
   exists in a customer database; HR_Master has no such table. */
IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.tables WHERE name = N'HR_UserMaster' AND schema_id = SCHEMA_ID(N'dbo'))
BEGIN
    RAISERROR(N'This script targets HR_Master (the tenant catalogue). The current database looks like a CUSTOMER database because dbo.HR_UserMaster exists. Aborting.', 16, 1);
    SET NOEXEC ON;
END
GO

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   1. HR_ClientRegistry - one row per customer.

   Created here only for a fresh catalogue; on existing servers the legacy app already created it
   and this block is skipped. Column names and types match what legacy reads.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.tables WHERE name = N'HR_ClientRegistry' AND schema_id = SCHEMA_ID(N'dbo'))
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE dbo.HR_ClientRegistry
    (
        ClientID         INT            IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,
        ClientCode       NVARCHAR(50)   NOT NULL,
        /* Legacy host:port resolution. Nullable because key-based resolution does not use it;
           kept so an un-upgraded legacy deployment on this catalogue still resolves by port. */
        HostName         NVARCHAR(200)  NULL,
        DatabaseName     NVARCHAR(128)  NOT NULL,
        /* Legacy-only. This API never reads it - it builds its own connection from
           MultiTenancy:ClientConnectionTemplate so SQL credentials stay out of the catalogue. */
        ConnectionString NVARCHAR(1000) NULL,
        IsActive         BIT            NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_HR_ClientRegistry_IsActive DEFAULT (1),
        CreatedOn        DATETIME2(0)   NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_HR_ClientRegistry_CreatedOn DEFAULT (SYSUTCDATETIME()),
        CONSTRAINT PK_HR_ClientRegistry PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (ClientID),
        CONSTRAINT UQ_HR_ClientRegistry_ClientCode UNIQUE (ClientCode)
    );
END
GO

/* SchemaVersion - highest applied migration for this tenant. Returned by /api/Tenant/Resolve so
   both applications can refuse to serve a tenant whose database is behind the build, instead of
   failing later with "Invalid column name" on one screen.

   Left NULL by this script. It is populated by the migration consolidation work, which is tracked
   separately - until then every caller must treat NULL as "unknown", never as "behind". */
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.columns WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID(N'dbo.HR_ClientRegistry') AND name = N'SchemaVersion')
BEGIN
    ALTER TABLE dbo.HR_ClientRegistry ADD SchemaVersion INT NULL;
END
GO

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2. HR_ClientProductKey - the keys a customer logs in with.

   A separate table rather than a column on the registry so a key can be rotated without downtime:
   issue the new one, let the customer switch, then revoke the old. Several active keys per client
   is normal during that window.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.tables WHERE name = N'HR_ClientProductKey' AND schema_id = SCHEMA_ID(N'dbo'))
BEGIN
    CREATE TABLE dbo.HR_ClientProductKey
    (
        ProductKeyID INT           IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL,
        ClientID     INT           NOT NULL,
        /* SHA-256 hex of the normalised 25-character payload. The key itself is NEVER stored:
           it selects a database, so it is a credential. A plain hash rather than bcrypt is
           deliberate - lookup must be one indexed equality match against an unknown tenant, and
           the input is 125 bits of uniform randomness, so there is no dictionary to run on it. */
        KeyHash      CHAR(64)      NOT NULL,
        /* Free text for the people issuing keys, e.g. "issued 2026-10-24, rotation of #3". */
        Label        NVARCHAR(100) NULL,
        IsActive     BIT           NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_HR_ClientProductKey_IsActive DEFAULT (1),
        CreatedOn    DATETIME2(0)  NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_HR_ClientProductKey_CreatedOn DEFAULT (SYSUTCDATETIME()),
        RevokedOn    DATETIME2(0)  NULL,
        CONSTRAINT PK_HR_ClientProductKey PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (ProductKeyID),
        /* One key maps to exactly one tenant, always. */
        CONSTRAINT UQ_HR_ClientProductKey_KeyHash UNIQUE (KeyHash),
        CONSTRAINT FK_HR_ClientProductKey_Client FOREIGN KEY (ClientID)
            REFERENCES dbo.HR_ClientRegistry (ClientID)
    );

    /* Login resolves by hash on every cache miss; this is the only lookup path that matters. */
    CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_HR_ClientProductKey_Lookup
        ON dbo.HR_ClientProductKey (KeyHash)
        INCLUDE (ClientID, IsActive, RevokedOn);
END
GO

SET NOEXEC OFF;
GO

/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   ONBOARDING A TENANT (run by hand until the service portal does it)

   1. The service portal provisions the database and hands back its name.
   2. Register the customer:

        INSERT INTO dbo.HR_ClientRegistry (ClientCode, DatabaseName, HostName, IsActive)
        VALUES (N'ACME', N'HR_ACME', NULL, 1);

   3. Generate a key with the application's own generator so the format and hash match exactly -
      do NOT invent one by hand. Either:
        - POST /api/Tenant/IssueKey (if that admin endpoint has been added), or
        - run SolutionOne_Core.MultiTenancy.ProductKey.Generate() / .NormalizeAndHash() in LINQPad
          or a scratch console project.

      It returns the display key (give this to the customer, once) and its hash (store this).

   4. Store ONLY the hash:

        INSERT INTO dbo.HR_ClientProductKey (ClientID, KeyHash, Label)
        SELECT ClientID, N'<64-hex-hash>', N'initial key'
        FROM dbo.HR_ClientRegistry WHERE ClientCode = N'ACME';

   5. Suspend a customer with:   UPDATE dbo.HR_ClientRegistry SET IsActive = 0 WHERE ClientCode = N'ACME';
      It takes effect within MultiTenancy:CacheMinutes (10 by default), on every request, not just
      at next login.

   6. Revoke a key with:         UPDATE dbo.HR_ClientProductKey SET IsActive = 0, RevokedOn = SYSUTCDATETIME() WHERE KeyHash = N'...';
      Also bounded by the cache period - revocation is not an instant kill switch. To cut access
      off immediately, suspend the tenant as well.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
EOF

# Spec — product-key tenant resolution in SolutionOneWeb (legacy payroll)

Implementation spec for the legacy side only. The API side is built and merged; nothing here
requires a change to it.

## Why

Legacy currently picks its database by **host:port** — `DbConnectionFactory.ResolveClientByHost`
matches `X-Forwarded-Host` / `Host` / `Request.Url.Authority` against `HR_ClientRegistry.HostName`,
which forces one public port per customer and silently falls back to `sqlConnectionString` when no
row matches. That fallback is the dangerous part: a proxy misconfiguration serves the wrong
customer's database with no error.

Replacement: legacy holds a **product key**, asks the API which database that key maps to, and
builds its connection from its own local template. One catalogue, one owner (the API), one
resolution rule for both applications.

Legacy also stops needing any rights on `HR_Master`, which removes the
`Cannot open database 'HR_Master' requested by the login` failure its own code documents.

## What legacy gets back — and what it does not

**Identity only. Never a connection string.** Both applications point at the same customer
database but connect with their own SQL logins, so the catalogue supplies only `DatabaseName` and
each app supplies its own credentials. SQL credentials never cross the network.

## 1. Web.config

```xml
<appSettings>
  <!-- Product key issued for this customer. Presence of a non-empty value is what switches
       resolution from host:port to key-based. -->
  <add key="ProductKey" value="SO1-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX" />

  <!-- Base URL of SolutionOneWebPortal_API, no trailing slash. HTTPS in production. -->
  <add key="TenantApiBaseUrl" value="https://api.example.com" />

  <!-- Optional. Default 10, matching the API's MultiTenancy:CacheMinutes. -->
  <add key="TenantApiCacheMinutes" value="10" />

  <!-- Optional. Default 5000 ms. Keep it short: this sits in front of every request on a
       cache miss. -->
  <add key="TenantApiTimeoutMs" value="5000" />

  <!-- Unchanged. Must stay true for any multi-tenant resolution to happen at all. -->
  <add key="EnableMultiTenant" value="true" />
</appSettings>
```

`clientConnectionTemplate` in `<connectionStrings>` is already present and keeps its current
meaning: server + credentials + options, with `Initial Catalog` replaced per tenant.

## 2. API contract

```
POST {TenantApiBaseUrl}/api/Tenant/Resolve
Content-Type: application/json

{ "productKey": "SO1-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX" }
```

**200**
```json
{
  "isSuccess": true,
  "status": 200,
  "message": "Tenant resolved.",
  "data": {
    "clientId": 7,
    "clientCode": "ACME",
    "databaseName": "HR_ACME",
    "isActive": true,
    "schemaVersion": null
  }
}
```

| Status | Meaning | Legacy should |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Resolved | Use `databaseName`; cache it |
| 401 | Key unknown or malformed | Fail the request. Do **not** fall back |
| 403 | Subscription suspended | Fail the request. Do **not** fall back |
| 404 | `MultiTenancy:Enabled` is false on the API | Fall back to host:port, then `sqlConnectionString` |
| 429 | Rate limited (10/min per IP) | Serve last-known-good from cache |
| 5xx / timeout | API unreachable | Serve last-known-good from cache; fail only if there is none |

`schemaVersion` is null until the migration consolidation lands. **Treat null as "unknown", never
as "behind"** — every tenant reads null today.

## 3. Code changes — `App_Code/DbConnectionFactory.cs`

One file. Public surface stays identical so no call site changes.

### 3a. New resolution branch

In `GetCurrentClient()`, before the existing host lookup:

```csharp
string productKey = ConfigurationManager.AppSettings["ProductKey"];
if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(productKey))
    return ResolveClientByProductKey(productKey);
// else fall through to the existing ResolveClientByHost path
```

Same insertion in `GetConnectionStringForSessionProvider()`. The key path reads no `Session`, so
that method gets simpler, not harder — it can call the same helper directly.

### 3b. `ResolveClientByProductKey`

- Cache key: `"Tenant_ByKey_" + productKey`, in `HttpRuntime.Cache`, TTL `TenantApiCacheMinutes`.
- On hit, return immediately.
- On miss, call the API and cache the result.
- On success, **also** store the `TenantClientInfo` under a second, never-expiring key
  (`"Tenant_LastGood_" + productKey`) — this is the outage fallback below.
- Populate `TenantClientInfo` as: `ClientID`, `ClientCode`, `DatabaseName` from the response;
  `HostName = null`; `ConnectionString = null` (so `BuildClientConnectionString` falls through to
  `clientConnectionTemplate`, which is exactly what we want — no change needed to that method).

### 3c. HTTP call — use `HttpWebRequest`, synchronously

`GetConnectionString()` is synchronous and called from everywhere, including page lifecycle
events. **Do not** use `HttpClient` with `.Result` / `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` — classic ASP.NET
has a `SynchronizationContext` and that deadlocks the request thread under load.

```csharp
var request = (HttpWebRequest)WebRequest.Create(baseUrl + "/api/Tenant/Resolve");
request.Method = "POST";
request.ContentType = "application/json";
request.Timeout = timeoutMs;          // connect + send
request.ReadWriteTimeout = timeoutMs; // response read
```

Write the JSON body, call `GetResponse()`, parse with `Newtonsoft.Json` (already in `Bin`, 13.0.1).
A non-200 arrives as `WebException` — read `((HttpWebResponse)ex.Response).StatusCode` to tell 401
from 503. Also ensure TLS 1.2 is enabled once at startup if the API is HTTPS:
`ServicePointManager.SecurityProtocol |= SecurityProtocolType.Tls12;`

### 3d. Availability — the fallback rule

Legacy now depends on the API for resolution, so an API outage must not take every customer down.

```
API reachable          → use the response, refresh both caches
API unreachable/5xx/429 → use "Tenant_LastGood_" entry if present
No last-good entry      → throw. Never fall back to sqlConnectionString.
```

That last line matters. Falling back to `sqlConnectionString` on an outage is exactly the bug this
change exists to remove — it would point a customer at whatever database the server was last
configured for. A clear error is correct; the wrong database is not.

A 401 or 403 is a **definitive** answer, not an outage: do not serve last-known-good for those.
Clear both cache entries so a revoked key stops working within one request.

### 3e. `GetActiveClients()`

Used by `DatabaseMigrationRunner.RunPendingForAllActiveClients()`. Under key-based resolution a
deployment serves exactly one customer, so return a single-element list containing the resolved
client. Do **not** keep querying `HR_ClientRegistry` directly — the point is that legacy no longer
touches `HR_Master`.

## 4. What must not change

- `BuildClientConnectionString` — already does the right thing; it falls through to
  `clientConnectionTemplate` when `ConnectionString` is null.
- `ClearTenantScopedSession` and its key list — still needed; a key change must still clear
  `UserID` / `CompanyID` / `FASYear` etc.
- `ClientDbSessionStateStoreProvider` — unchanged, it just calls
  `GetConnectionStringForSessionProvider()`.
- `EnableMultiTenant = false` — must still mean "single database, never open the catalogue".
- SignIn, `UserSessionHelper`, `JwtHelper`, company selection — all out of scope for this phase.
- `DatabaseMigrationRunner`'s auto-run behaviour — being handled separately by the migration
  consolidation work.

## 5. Testing

1. `EnableMultiTenant=false` → unchanged behaviour, no API calls. Regression check first.
2. `EnableMultiTenant=true` + valid `ProductKey` → `TenantCheck.ashx?key=tenantdiag` shows the
   resolved database. Extend its diagnostics to print the resolution source (key vs host) and
   whether the answer came from cache.
3. Wrong key → clean error, and confirm via SQL Profiler that **no** connection is opened to
   `sqlConnectionString`'s database.
4. Stop the API, then browse → pages still work from last-known-good.
5. Stop the API and clear `HttpRuntime.Cache` (recycle the pool) → clean error, not a wrong-database
   connection. This is the one people get wrong.
6. Suspend the tenant (`UPDATE HR_ClientRegistry SET IsActive = 0`) → access stops within the cache
   period.
7. Two deployments, two keys, same server → confirm each resolves to its own database and that
   nothing changes when the ports are swapped (proving host:port is no longer load-bearing).

## 6. Rollout

Per server: deploy the build with `ProductKey` **blank** first (behaviour is byte-identical to
today), then fill the key in `Web.config`. That edit recycles the app pool and signs users out, so
do it out of hours. Rolling back is removing the key again — no database change is involved.
MDEOF

content.text:
Done. The catalogue and key switch are built, and the legacy spec is written.

## The switch

Exactly what I argued for — three constructor changes, **zero repository files touched**:

| Injection point | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `HrmsystemContext` (133 repos) | fixed string baked in at startup | `AddDbContext<>((sp, options) => ...)` reading `ITenantContext` per scope |
| `IDapperContext` (47 repos) | read + decrypted appsettings itself | takes `ITenantContext` |
| `DbConnectionConfig` (2 PMS repos) | **singleton** | scoped, from `ITenantContext` |

`ITenantContext.ConnectionString` throws rather than returning a default. `GlobalExceptionHandler` maps that to 401, so a request with no tenant gets a clean "sign in again", never another customer's data.

## Flow

```
POST /api/Login/LoginAuthentication { productKey, userName, passwordHash }
  → SHA-256 the normalised key → HR_ClientProductKey → HR_ClientRegistry
  → bind tenant → open THAT database → check the password there
  → JWT carries tenant_id

every later request: tenant from the signed claim only, never from the body again
```

`TenantResolutionMiddleware` sits after `UseAuthentication`. **Claim always wins** over the `X-Product-Key` header — that's what stops a signed-in user redirecting their session with someone else's key.

## Cache leak — bigger than I first reported

My first audit only covered the DAL. Sweeping BLL and the API found more, including constant keys:

- `EmailProviderSettingService` / `GraphMailSettingService` — `"email_active_provider"`, `"email_smtp_runtime_settings"`. **No tenant component at all** — tenant B would have sent mail through tenant A's provider and SMTP credentials.
- `PermissionChecker`, `PermissionAttribute` — `UserPermissions_{id}`, `PermissionVersion_{id}`
- `SystemSettingService`, `TravelPaymentService` — keyed on `CompanyMasterId`, which collides across databases

13 files now take `ITenantCache`, which prefixes keys so no call site can forget. Two keep raw `IMemoryCache` deliberately, both annotated: `LocationService` (external geo data, correctly shared) and `RbacManagementController` (compacts the whole process cache).

`MapperDecoratorReposiroty`'s static dictionary is **safe** — it caches compiled lambdas keyed on CLR type + column names, no tenant data. Separately, it's a non-thread-safe `Dictionary` mutated concurrently; pre-existing, untouched.

## Background work

`StartupTaskRunnerHostedService` and `ResumeProcessingWorker` had no tenant and would have thrown on first query. New `ITenantScopeRunner` gives them bound scopes — startup tasks run once per active tenant, and resume jobs are stamped with `ClientId` at enqueue (one shared queue, jobs from different customers interleave, so the binding has to ride on the job). `ResumeBatchCleanupWorker` needed nothing — in-memory store and filesystem only.

## Also fixed

`HrmsystemContext.OnConfiguring` had its check inverted — `if (optionsBuilder.IsConfigured)` *re-applied* the appsettings connection on top of already-configured options. Under multi-tenancy that would have silently discarded the tenant connection on every request.

## Not verified

**I haven't compiled or run any of this** — per your standing preference. Worth watching for on first build: the `const` interpolated SQL in `TenantRegistry` (needs C# 10+, fine on net8.0), and the `ITenantCache` swap across 13 files. Both are comments. Traced the whole path — here's the honest answer.

## Yes, with one caveat and one visible change

With `MultiTenancy:Enabled = false` (what's in `appsettings.json` now), every tenant code path short-circuits before it can touch anything:

| Component | Single-tenant behaviour |
|---|---|
| `TenantContext.ConnectionString` | returns decrypted `WebPortalConnectionString` — same string as before |
| `TenantResolutionMiddleware` | first line: `if (IsSingleTenantMode) { next(); return; }` — catalogue never opened |
| `LoginController` | `BindFromProductKeyAsync` returns `SingleTenant`, product key ignored entirely |
| JWT claims | `if (_tenantContext.Tenant is not null)` → null, so **no tenant claims added** — existing tokens stay valid |
| `ITenantCache` | prefix is the constant `"t0::"` |
| `TenantScopeRunner` | one unbound scope, runs once — identical to the old `CreateScope()` |
| `/api/Tenant/Resolve` | returns 404 "not enabled"; nothing calls it |

`HR_Master` is never contacted. `MasterConnectionString` and `ClientConnectionTemplate` being blank is fine — the startup validation that requires them only runs when `Enabled` is true.

## I found and fixed a real regression while checking this

Worth telling you because it would have bitten exactly the scenario you asked about. When I restructured `Program.cs` I'd dropped the `if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(decryptedConnectionString))` guard around the Serilog block. If decryption ever returned empty, `WriteTo.MSSqlServer(connectionString: null)` would throw **at startup** — app wouldn't boot. Guard is back; only Serilog needs it now, since the DbContext no longer depends on that block running.

I also verified `ApplicationSession` singleton→scoped is safe: all ~15 consumers are scoped services and repositories, nothing singleton injects it. A singleton consuming it would have failed DI validation at startup.

## One change you'll see

The login screen now has a **"Product Key"** field. It's not required and the server ignores it in single-tenant mode, but it's visible to your users today. If you'd rather it stay hidden until you go multi-tenant, say so — it's a one-line `*ngIf` and I'd need a flag from the backend to drive it.

## What I can't promise

**It hasn't been compiled.** That's the caveat. The runtime logic is traced and sound; what I can't rule out is a compile error. The biggest surface is the `ITenantCache` swap across 13 files — I enumerated every cache member call in them and it's only four (`Set`, `TryGetValue`, `Remove`, `GetOrCreateAsync`), all on the interface, so I'd expect it clean. Other spots worth watching on first build:

- `SolutionOne_Tests/RbacPermissionValidationTests.cs` — I rewrote its `new DapperContext(config)` call
- `ResumeParsingController` — new `ITenantContext` constructor parameter
- `const string sql = $@"..."` in `TenantRegistry` — needs C# 10+ constant interpolation, fine on net8.0

Run a build and paste anything that comes out; I'll fix it. If it compiles, run it against your default DB — behaviour should be indistinguishable from before apart from that login field.

content.text: <total_tokens>14975798 tokens left</total_tokens>

Both done.

## Product key as a separate flow

Removed the always-visible key field and made it a deliberate path:

```
Standard login                    Product key login
──────────────                    ─────────────────
Employee Code                     Step 1:  [SO1-XXXXX-XXXXX-...]  → Continue
Password                                   ↓ POST /api/Tenant/Verify
[Login]                           Step 2:  ✓ ACME          [Change]
                                           Employee Code
🔑 Sign in with a Product Key →            Password
                                           [Login]
```

Verifying the key *before* asking for credentials is the point of the two steps — a mistyped key comes back as "Invalid product key" immediately, instead of surfacing after they've typed a password as what reads like "wrong password". Step 2 names the organisation so they can see they're signing in to the right one.

**New endpoint: `POST /api/Tenant/Verify`.** I didn't reuse `Resolve` because it returns `databaseName`, which a browser has no business seeing. `Verify` returns only `{ requiresProductKey, clientCode }`, same rate-limit policy. If the server is single-tenant it answers `requiresProductKey: false` and the UI drops back to standard login rather than stranding someone on a step that can't complete.

Other behaviour:
- A browser that's used a key before **opens on the key step with it prefilled** — one tap on Continue. A browser that hasn't sees exactly today's login.
- Standard mode sends `productKey: ''`, so your current default-DB login is untouched.
- Added `/api/Tenant/` to the interceptor bypass. Without it a 401 from a wrong key fell through to the generic handler and showed "You do not have permission" on top of my own message.

## Mobile

The root cause wasn't styling, it was the layout row's inline `height: 100vh; overflow: hidden` — on a phone that clipped the form the moment the keyboard opened, with no way to scroll to it.

Worth noting: the `html, body { overflow: hidden }` rules in the SCSS were already **dead code**. Angular scopes component styles, so they compiled to `html[_ngcontent-x]` and never matched. The inline style was doing the damage.

Fixes:
- `min-height: 100dvh` (with `100vh` fallback) — `vh` doesn't track the mobile URL bar, so `100vh` content sits partly under it on iOS
- Branding panel hidden below `lg` — it would push the form below the fold
- **Inputs at 16px.** iOS Safari auto-zooms on focus for anything smaller; at the old 14px you ended up zoomed and scrolled sideways after tapping Password
- Buttons `min-height: 44px` (was ~30px from `padding: 6px`)
- Support bar wraps and recentres — four phone numbers on one line is far wider than a phone viewport
- Form top-aligns on mobile so fields stay reachable when the keyboard shrinks the viewport
- Landscape-phone breakpoint that shrinks the logo, since there's almost no vertical room
- Key field is monospace with letter-spacing — these get read off paper, and a mistyped character should be findable

`src/index.html` already had the right viewport meta, so nothing needed there.

## Not verified

Not built or opened in a browser. The template bindings all resolve against the component (checked), braces balance, and the old class names weren't used anywhere outside this component. What I can't confirm without running it is how it actually *looks* at each breakpoint — worth a pass in device emulation, particularly the 320px width and the landscape case.

One thing you may want to change: I kept `DxScrollViewModule` and `DxFormModule` in the component's imports even though the template doesn't use them. Harmless, but newer Angular emits an unused-import warning — say the word and I'll drop them.

cat > /home/rudy/docs/office/subscription_portal/BE/SubscriptionPortal.DataAccessLayer/SqlScripts/HrmsTemplate/generate-template.py << 'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generates the HRMS tenant-template scripts from a REFERENCE database.

    python3 generate-template.py --server 127.0.0.1 --database HRMS_REFERENCE \
        --user sa --password '***' --out ./out

Produces, in --out:
    01_schema.sql         every table/constraint/index/procedure/function/view, no data
    02_master_data.sql    rows for the tables in seed-tables.txt, in file order
    03_baseline_stamp.sql marks HR_SchemaMigrationHistory so the migration runner skips what
                          the baseline already contains

The provisioning service creates the database itself (so it controls name, collation and file
paths) and then runs these three in order. None of them contains CREATE DATABASE, USE, or SQLCMD
directives, because ADO.NET cannot execute SQLCMD mode - only GO batch separation is needed, which
the runner already does.

Why a generated script instead of RESTORE of a .bak:
  - a backup carries whatever was in the source database, including the source customer's data
  - a backup cannot be reviewed or diffed in source control
  - RESTORE needs the file on the SQL Server's own disk, which rules out managed/cloud SQL
  - a generated CREATE pins the collation explicitly rather than inheriting it by accident
"""
import argparse, json, os, re, subprocess, sys

  - a backup carries whatever was in the source database, including the source customer's data
  - a backup cannot be reviewed or diffed in source control
  - RESTORE needs the file on the SQL Server's own disk, which rules out managed/cloud SQL
  - a generated CREATE pins the collation explicitly rather than inheriting it by accident
"""
import argparse, json, os, re, subprocess, sys

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def sqlcmd(args, query, database=None):
    cmd = ['sqlcmd', '-S', args.server, '-U', args.user, '-C', '-h', '-1', '-W', '-Y', '0',
           '-d', database or args.database, '-Q', query]
    env = dict(os.environ, SQLCMDPASSWORD=args.password)
    p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"sqlcmd failed:\n{p.stdout}\n{p.stderr}")
    return p.stdout


def query_json(args, query):
    """FOR JSON keeps SQL Server responsible for escaping, instead of us guessing at a delimiter."""
    raw = sqlcmd(args, f"SET NOCOUNT ON; {query} FOR JSON PATH, INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES")
    # sqlcmd splits long JSON across lines at a fixed width; rejoin before parsing.
    text = ''.join(line.strip() for line in raw.splitlines()
                   if line.strip() and not line.startswith('('))
    return json.loads(text) if text else []


def read_list(name):
    path = os.path.join(HERE, name)
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return []
    out = []
    for line in open(path):
        line = line.strip()
        if line and not line.startswith('#'):
            out.append(line)
    return out


def literal(value, sqltype):
    if value is None:
        return 'NULL'
    t = (sqltype or '').lower()
    if t in ('bit',):
        return '1' if value in (True, 1, '1', 'True', 'true') else '0'
    if t in ('int', 'bigint', 'smallint', 'tinyint', 'decimal', 'numeric',
             'float', 'real', 'money', 'smallmoney'):
        return str(value)
    if t in ('varbinary', 'binary', 'image', 'timestamp', 'rowversion'):
        # Base64 from FOR JSON; emit as NULL rather than guessing. No allowlisted table has one.
        return 'NULL'
    escaped = str(value).replace("'", "''")
    return f"N'{escaped}'"


def generate_schema(args, outdir):
    """sqlpackage extracts a .dacpac, then scripts it as a full CREATE for a fresh database."""
    dacpac = os.path.join(outdir, 'hrms_template.dacpac')
    conn = (f"Data Source={args.server};Initial Catalog={args.database};"
            f"User ID={args.user};Password={args.password};TrustServerCertificate=True")

    subprocess.run(['sqlpackage', '/Action:Extract', f'/SourceConnectionString:{conn}',
                    f'/TargetFile:{dacpac}', '/p:ExtractAllTableData=false',
                    '/p:IgnorePermissions=true', '/p:IgnoreUserLoginMappings=true',
                    '/p:VerifyExtraction=false'], check=True)

    raw = os.path.join(outdir, '_schema_raw.sql')
    subprocess.run(['sqlpackage', '/Action:Script', f'/SourceFile:{dacpac}',
                    f'/TargetServerName:{args.server}', '/TargetDatabaseName:__TEMPLATE_PROBE__',
                    f'/TargetUser:{args.user}', f'/TargetPassword:{args.password}',
                    '/TargetTrustServerCertificate:true', f'/OutputPath:{raw}',
                    '/p:CreateNewDatabase=true', '/p:ScriptDatabaseOptions=false',
                    '/p:IgnorePermissions=true', '/p:IgnoreUserSettingsObjects=true'], check=True)

    return strip_sqlcmd(raw, os.path.join(outdir, '01_schema.sql'),
                        read_list('drop-tables.txt'))


def strip_sqlcmd(raw_path, out_path, excluded_tables):
    """
    Turns sqlpackage's SQLCMD-mode publish script into plain T-SQL the provisioning service can
    execute over ADO.NET: drops :setvar/:on error/GOTO-style directives, the CREATE DATABASE and
    ALTER DATABASE preamble (the service creates the database itself), and any statement touching
    a table named in drop-tables.txt.
    """
    text = open(raw_path, encoding='utf-8-sig').read()
    batches = re.split(r'(?mi)^\s*GO\s*$', text)

    skip_markers = (':setvar', ':on error', ':r ', '$(DatabaseName)', '$(DefaultDataPath)',
                    '__IsSqlCmdEnabled', 'SET NOEXEC')
    kept = []
    for batch in batches:
        s = batch.strip()
        if not s:
            continue
        if any(m in s for m in skip_markers):
            continue
        if re.search(r'(?i)\b(CREATE|ALTER)\s+DATABASE\b', s):
            continue
        if re.match(r'(?i)^\s*USE\s+', s):
            continue
        if re.match(r'(?i)^\s*PRINT\s+', s):
            continue
        if excluded_tables and re.search(
                r'(?i)\[(' + '|'.join(re.escape(t) for t in excluded_tables) + r')\]', s):
            continue
        kept.append(s)

    with open(out_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write("/* HRMS tenant template - SCHEMA ONLY. Generated by generate-template.py.\n"
                "   Run against an ALREADY-CREATED, empty database. Contains no CREATE DATABASE:\n"
                "   the provisioning service creates it so it can pin the collation and file paths. */\n\n")
        for b in kept:
            f.write(b + "\nGO\n")
    return len(kept)


def generate_master_data(args, outdir):
    tables = read_list('seed-tables.txt')
    written, skipped, total_rows = [], [], 0

    with open(os.path.join(outdir, '02_master_data.sql'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write("/* HRMS tenant template - MASTER DATA. Generated by generate-template.py.\n"
                "   Allowlisted in seed-tables.txt; every other table is left empty on purpose.\n"
                "   Emitted in allowlist order so parent rows land before their foreign keys. */\n\n")

        for table in tables:
            exists = sqlcmd(args, f"SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT OBJECT_ID('dbo.{table}')").strip()
            if not exists or exists.upper().startswith('NULL'):
                skipped.append(f"{table} (no such table)")
                continue

            cols = query_json(args, f"""
                SELECT c.name AS name, t.name AS type, c.is_identity AS is_identity,
                       c.is_computed AS is_computed
                FROM sys.columns c
                JOIN sys.types t ON t.user_type_id = c.user_type_id
                WHERE c.object_id = OBJECT_ID('dbo.{table}')
                ORDER BY c.column_id""")
            # Computed columns cannot be inserted into.
            cols = [c for c in cols if not c['is_computed']]
            if not cols:
                skipped.append(f"{table} (no insertable columns)")
                continue

            names = [c['name'] for c in cols]
            rows = query_json(args, f"SELECT {', '.join('[' + n + ']' for n in names)} FROM dbo.{table}")
            if not rows:
                skipped.append(f"{table} (empty)")
                continue

            has_identity = any(c['is_identity'] for c in cols)
            types = {c['name']: c['type'] for c in cols}

            f.write(f"\n/* ---- {table} ({len(rows)} rows) ---- */\n")
            # Idempotent: re-running the template must not duplicate the menu.
            f.write(f"IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.{table})\nBEGIN\n")
            if has_identity:
                f.write(f"    SET IDENTITY_INSERT dbo.{table} ON;\n")
            collist = ', '.join(f'[{n}]' for n in names)
            for row in rows:
                vals = ', '.join(literal(row.get(n), types[n]) for n in names)
                f.write(f"    INSERT INTO dbo.{table} ({collist}) VALUES ({vals});\n")
            if has_identity:
                f.write(f"    SET IDENTITY_INSERT dbo.{table} OFF;\n")
            f.write("END\nGO\n")

            written.append(f"{table} ({len(rows)})")
            total_rows += len(rows)

    return written, skipped, total_rows


def generate_stamp(args, outdir):
    """
    Records every migration the baseline already contains, so the HRMS migration runner starts
    from the right point instead of replaying 236 scripts against a schema that already has them.
    """
    rows = query_json(args, "SELECT MigrationID AS id, ScriptName AS script FROM dbo.HR_SchemaMigrationHistory")
    path = os.path.join(outdir, '03_baseline_stamp.sql')
    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write("/* HRMS tenant template - BASELINE MIGRATION STAMP. Generated by generate-template.py.\n"
                "   The schema in 01_schema.sql already includes everything these migrations did, so they\n"
                "   are marked applied. Without this the runner replays them all against a database that\n"
                "   already has the columns, and stops at the first one that errors. */\n\n")
        f.write("IF OBJECT_ID('dbo.HR_SchemaMigrationHistory') IS NULL\n"
                "BEGIN\n"
                "    CREATE TABLE dbo.HR_SchemaMigrationHistory (\n"
                "        MigrationID NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,\n"
                "        ScriptName  NVARCHAR(300) NOT NULL,\n"
                "        AppliedOn   DATETIME      NOT NULL CONSTRAINT DF_HR_SchemaMigrationHistory_AppliedOn DEFAULT (GETDATE()),\n"
                "        AppliedBy   NVARCHAR(100) NULL,\n"
                "        Checksum    NVARCHAR(100) NULL,\n"
                "        CONSTRAINT PK_HR_SchemaMigrationHistory PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (MigrationID)\n"
                "    );\n"
                "END\nGO\n\n")
        for r in rows:
            mid = str(r['id']).replace("'", "''")
            script = str(r.get('script') or r['id']).replace("'", "''")
            f.write(f"IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.HR_SchemaMigrationHistory WHERE MigrationID = N'{mid}')\n"
                    f"    INSERT INTO dbo.HR_SchemaMigrationHistory (MigrationID, ScriptName, AppliedBy)\n"
                    f"    VALUES (N'{mid}', N'{script}', N'baseline');\n")
        f.write("GO\n")
    return len(rows)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument('--server', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--database', required=True, help='clean REFERENCE database to generate from')
    ap.add_argument('--user', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--password', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--out', default=os.path.join(HERE, 'out'))
    ap.add_argument('--skip-schema', action='store_true', help='regenerate data/stamp only')
    args = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)

    if not args.skip_schema:
        batches = generate_schema(args, args.out)
        print(f"01_schema.sql        : {batches} batches")

    written, skipped, rows = generate_master_data(args, args.out)
    print(f"02_master_data.sql   : {len(written)} tables, {rows} rows")
    for w in written:
        print(f"    seeded  {w}")
    for s in skipped:
        print(f"    skipped {s}")

    count = generate_stamp(args, args.out)
    print(f"03_baseline_stamp.sql: {count} migrations stamped")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

p = 'generate-template.py'
s = open(p).read()

# ---- sqlcmd: widen output -------------------------------------------------
old = """    cmd = ['sqlcmd', '-S', args.server, '-U', args.user, '-C', '-h', '-1', '-W', '-Y', '0',

new = """    # -y 0 / -Y 0: do not truncate wide columns. These are sqlcmd display options, not server
    # features, so they are safe against any server version. Without -y 0 the generated INSERT
    # text is silently cut at 256 characters.
    cmd = ['sqlcmd', '-S', args.server, '-U', args.user, '-C', '-h', '-1', '-W',
           '-y', '0', '-Y', '0', '-d', database or args.database, '-Q', query]"""
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

# ---- replace the FOR JSON helper with a 2012-safe delimited reader --------
old = '''def query_json(args, query):
    """FOR JSON keeps SQL Server responsible for escaping, instead of us guessing at a delimiter."""
    raw = sqlcmd(args, f"SET NOCOUNT ON; {query} FOR JSON PATH, INCLUDE_NULL_VALUES")
    # sqlcmd splits long JSON across lines at a fixed width; rejoin before parsing.
    text = ''.join(line.strip() for line in raw.splitlines()
                   if line.strip() and not line.startswith('('))

new = '''def query_lines(args, query):
    """
    Runs a query whose result is ONE already-formatted text column, and returns its lines.

    Deliberately not FOR JSON: that is SQL Server 2016+, and both this generator and everything it
    produces have to work against SQL Server 2012 (the reference database runs at compatibility
    level 110, and customer servers are older than this build machine).
    """
    raw = sqlcmd(args, f"SET NOCOUNT ON; {query}")
    out = []
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        line = line.rstrip()
        if not line or line.startswith('(') or line.strip() == 'NULL':
            continue
        out.append(line)
    return out


def column_metadata(args, table):
    """name / type / is_identity per column, oldest-safe catalog query, pipe-delimited."""
    rows = query_lines(args, f"""
        SELECT c.name + '|' + t.name + '|' + CONVERT(varchar(1), c.is_identity)
        FROM sys.columns c
        JOIN sys.types t ON t.user_type_id = c.user_type_id
        WHERE c.object_id = OBJECT_ID('dbo.{table}')
          AND c.is_computed = 0
        ORDER BY c.column_id""")
    cols = []
    for r in rows:
        parts = r.split('|')
        if len(parts) >= 3:
            cols.append({'name': parts[0].strip(), 'type': parts[1].strip(),
                         'is_identity': parts[2].strip() == '1'})
    return cols

    """
    T-SQL that renders one column as a literal for an INSERT, evaluated BY THE SERVER.

    Escaping is done with REPLACE(x, '''', ''''''), not QUOTENAME: QUOTENAME is limited to 128

    (HR_EmailTemplate, HR_ReportLayout) instead of failing loudly.
    """
    n, t = col['name'], col['type'].lower()

    if t in ('int', 'bigint', 'smallint', 'tinyint', 'decimal', 'numeric',
             'float', 'real', 'money', 'smallmoney'):
        return f"ISNULL(CONVERT(varchar(50), [{n}]), 'NULL')"
    if t == 'bit':
        return f"ISNULL(CONVERT(varchar(1), CONVERT(tinyint, [{n}])), 'NULL')"
    if t in ('date', 'datetime', 'datetime2', 'smalldatetime', 'time', 'datetimeoffset'):

        return f"ISNULL('''' + CONVERT(varchar(33), [{n}], 126) + '''', 'NULL')"

    if t in ('varbinary', 'binary', 'image', 'timestamp', 'rowversion'):
        # No allowlisted table has one; emitted as NULL rather than guessed at.
        return "'NULL'"
    # Everything textual. N-prefixed so unicode survives on a non-unicode default collation.
    return f"ISNULL('N''' + REPLACE(CONVERT(nvarchar(max), [{n}]), '''', '''''') + '''', 'NULL')"'''
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p = 'generate-template.py'
s = open(p).read()

# 1. -b: without it sqlcmd exits 0 on a T-SQL error and the error TEXT is captured as if it were
#    data. That is exactly how "HR_MenuItems (2 rows)" happened for a 264-row table.
old = """    cmd = ['sqlcmd', '-S', args.server, '-U', args.user, '-C', '-h', '-1', '-W',
           '-y', '0', '-Y', '0', '-d', database or args.database, '-Q', query]"""
new = """    # -b makes sqlcmd exit non-zero on a T-SQL error. Without it an error is printed to stdout,
    # exit code stays 0, and the error text is silently captured as though it were a result row.
    # -y 0 / -Y 0 stop wide columns being truncated at 256 characters. All three are client
    # options, not server features, so they are safe against any server version.
    cmd = ['sqlcmd', '-S', args.server, '-U', args.user, '-C', '-b', '-h', '-1', '-W',
           '-y', '0', '-Y', '0', '-d', database or args.database, '-Q', query]"""
assert old in s, "cmd line"
s = s.replace(old, new, 1)

# 2. the text branch built 'N'''' (five quotes = unterminated literal) instead of 'N''' .
old_txt = """    # Everything textual. N-prefixed so unicode survives a non-unicode default collation.
    return ("ISNULL('N" + quote + " + REPLACE(CONVERT(nvarchar(max), [" + n + "]), "
            + quote + ", " + doubled + ") + " + quote + ", 'NULL')")"""
new_txt = """    # Everything textual. N-prefixed so unicode survives a non-unicode default collation.
    # n_prefix is the T-SQL source for the two characters  N'  - note THREE trailing quotes, not
    # four: 'N''' opens a literal, emits N, emits one escaped quote, closes. Writing 'N'''' leaves
    # the literal unterminated and the whole SELECT fails to parse.
    n_prefix = "'N'''"
    return ("ISNULL(" + n_prefix + " + REPLACE(CONVERT(nvarchar(max), [" + n + "]), "
            + quote + ", " + doubled + ") + " + quote + ", 'NULL')")"""
assert old_txt in s, "text branch"
s = s.replace(old_txt, new_txt, 1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("patched")

p = 'generate-template.py'

           '-y', '0', '-Y', '0', '-d', database or args.database, '-Q', query]"""
new = """    # -b   exit non-zero on a T-SQL error. Without it an error prints to stdout, the exit code
    #      stays 0, and the error text is silently captured as though it were a result row.
    # -y 0 do not truncate wide columns at 256 characters.
    # -w   output line width. This one matters: at the default width sqlcmd WRAPS a long row onto
    #      several lines, and a newline landing inside a generated string literal silently changes
    #      the data being seeded. 65535 is the maximum; generate_master_data additionally checks
    #      the emitted line count against COUNT(*) so any row still long enough to wrap is caught
    #      rather than written out corrupted.
    # All of these are client options, not server features, so they are safe against any server.
    cmd = ['sqlcmd', '-S', args.server, '-U', args.user, '-C', '-b', '-h', '-1', '-W',
           '-y', '0', '-Y', '0', '-w', '65535',
           '-d', database or args.database, '-Q', query]"""

            if not rows:
                skipped.append(table + " (empty)")

                                   + table).strip() or 0)
            if expected == 0:
                skipped.append(table + " (empty)")
                continue

            rows = query_lines(args, select)

            # One output line per row, or the data is not what it appears to be. A mismatch means
            # sqlcmd wrapped a row that exceeded the output width, which inserts newlines inside
            # string literals - the seeded value would differ from the source silently. Fail here
            # instead of writing a corrupted template.
            if len(rows) != expected:
                raise SystemExit(
                    "Row count mismatch for " + table + ": expected " + str(expected)
                    + " rows but got " + str(len(rows)) + " output lines.\\n"
                    "A row is almost certainly longer than the 65535-character output width.\\n"
                    "Seed this table from a hand-written script instead, and remove it from "
                    "seed-tables.txt.")"""
assert old2 in s

cat > /home/rudy/docs/office/subscription_portal/BE/SubscriptionPortal.DataAccessLayer/SqlScripts/HrmsTemplate/README.md << 'MDEOF'
# HRMS tenant template

Replaces `RESTORE DATABASE` from a `.bak` with a generated, reviewable schema + master-data script.

## Why this replaces the backup

`DatabaseProvisioningService.RestoreTemplateAsync` restores
`HRMS_Subscription_Use_13102026.bak`. Four problems, in order of severity:

1. **The template carries a real customer's data.** The reference database this was generated from
   (`HRMS_DEVITURNOMATICS`) contains one `Company` row — *DEVI TURNOMATICS PRIVATE LIMITED* — plus
   408 employees, 14 users and 147,825 attendance rows. If the `.bak` is a backup of that database
   or one like it, **every tenant provisioned so far received another customer's HR data**. Verify
   what is actually in that `.bak` before provisioning anything else.
2. **It cannot be reviewed.** A `.bak` is opaque to code review, diffing and source control. Nobody
   can tell what a new tenant will contain without restoring it and looking.
3. **It needs filesystem access on the SQL Server itself.** `RESTORE ... FROM DISK` reads a path on
   the database server, not the API host. That rules out Azure SQL and any managed instance, and
   couples provisioning to one machine's directory layout.
4. **Collation is inherited by accident.** The reference database is `Latin1_General_CI_AI`
   (accent-*insensitive*) while the server default is `SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS`
   (accent-*sensitive*). A plain `CREATE DATABASE` would silently get the server default and change
   string-matching behaviour; cross-database joins then fail outright with
   `Cannot resolve collation conflict`. The generated script pins the collation explicitly.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `generate-template.py` | Regenerates everything below from a reference database |
| `seed-tables.txt` | **Allowlist** of tables whose rows are copied into a new tenant |
| `drop-tables.txt` | Tables excluded from the schema (one customer's scratch tables) |
| `out/01_schema.sql` | 314 tables, 85 procedures, 4 functions, 1 view, 163 indexes. No data |
| `out/02_master_data.sql` | 1,279 rows across 28 tables — menus, RBAC catalogue, templates, lookups |
| `out/03_baseline_stamp.sql` | Marks the 224 migrations the baseline already contains |

### Why an allowlist and not an exclusion list

Seeding is opt-in. Any table added to the HRMS later is **empty** in a new tenant until someone
deliberately lists it. With an exclusion list the default is the opposite: a new table is copied
until someone remembers to exclude it, and the first time that table holds customer data every new
tenant receives it. A missing lookup list is a bug report; the other way round is a breach.

## Regenerating

Needs `sqlcmd` and `sqlpackage` (`dotnet tool install -g microsoft.sqlpackage`).

```bash
python3 generate-template.py \
    --server 127.0.0.1 --database HRMS_REFERENCE \
    --user sa --password '***' --out ./out
```

Point `--database` at a **clean reference database**, never at a live customer's. The generator
copies every row of every allowlisted table verbatim.

It verifies each table's recovered row count against `COUNT(*)` and aborts on a mismatch, so a row
too long for the output width fails loudly instead of seeding truncated data.

### SQL Server 2012 compatibility

Both the generator and its output target SQL Server 2012. The generator uses no `FOR JSON`
(2016+); row extraction is done with server-side string concatenation and a `/*#EOR#*/` sentinel.
The generated schema was checked for `TRIM()` (2017+), `DROP ... IF EXISTS`, `CREATE OR ALTER`,
`STRING_AGG`, `STRING_SPLIT`, `OPENJSON`, temporal tables and scoped configuration — none present.
The only `STRING_SPLIT` in the codebase is inside a comment explaining it was avoided because
"production is 2014".

If you regenerate against a newer source server, re-run those checks.

## Wiring into provisioning

Replace `RestoreTemplateAsync` with four steps. The service already does step 5.

```
1. CREATE DATABASE [name] COLLATE Latin1_General_CI_AI
2. run out/01_schema.sql
3. run out/02_master_data.sql
4. run out/03_baseline_stamp.sql
5. SeedAdminUserAsync(...)   <- unchanged, already seeds Company + admin
```

Notes for the implementation:

- **Collation must be explicit** in step 1, for the reason above.
- **Split on `GO` before executing.** `GO` is a sqlcmd batch separator, not T-SQL, and ADO.NET
  rejects it. `SolutionOneWeb/App_Code/DatabaseMigrationRunner.cs` already has a `GoBatchRegex`
  that handles this correctly, including `GO` followed by a comment — reuse that regex rather than
  splitting on the bare string, or a `GO` inside a string literal will split a statement in half.
- **Do not wrap the whole thing in one transaction.** Several `CREATE PROCEDURE` batches must be
  the first statement in their batch, and a single transaction over 19,000 lines of DDL will
  escalate locks badly. The existing cleanup path (`TryDropDatabaseAsync` on failure) is the right
  rollback: drop the half-built database and report.
- **Keep the scripts as embedded resources or content files** so they deploy with the API, rather
  than as a path on the database server — that is the coupling being removed.
- Step 4 matters: without it the HRMS migration runner replays all 224 migrations against a schema
  that already has them, stops at the first error, and the tenant silently ends up part-migrated.

## Known gaps

- `Country` and `Currency` are allowlisted but **empty in the reference database**, so they seed
  nothing today. If the HRMS expects them populated, seed them from a hand-written script.
- `varbinary` columns are emitted as `NULL`. No allowlisted table currently has one; if one is
  added, the generator needs a binary-literal path.
- The customer's own masters (departments, designations, shifts, holidays, leave types, salary
  heads) are deliberately **not** seeded. If a new tenant should start with a generic starter set
  rather than nothing, that is a separate, hand-written `04_starter_data.sql` — do not solve it by
  copying one customer's rows into the allowlist.
MDEOF
